script.title: Gross Total Income vs Total Income
script.caption_hook: Tax is charged on the lower income, not your full income!

lines.say: Wait, tax isn't charged on my full income?
Right. Tax is charged on Total Income, which can be lower than Gross Total Income. Let's see how we get there.
So how do we get GTI first?
First, find income under each head. Then do clubbing and set-off of losses. Adding up gives Gross Total Income, or GTI.
Okay, and where do deductions come in?
Only after GTI. Chapter VI-A deductions allowed are cut from GTI. What is left is Total Income.
Can you show a quick number example?
Sure. Income from salary, after standard deduction, is ₹6,00,000. Income from house property is ₹1,00,000. So GTI is ₹7,00,000.
What if my Chapter VI-A deductions allowed are ₹1,00,000?
Then Total Income is ₹7,00,000 minus ₹1,00,000, so ₹6,00,000. Tax rates apply on that figure.
Hmm, what about exempt income, like agricultural income?
Exempt income stays out of both GTI and Total Income.
Oh, got it! Gross first, then Total.
Yes. Gross is the garden, Total is the trimmed.

check_notes: Writer: Line 8: examiner suggested house property ₹50,000, but that gives ₹6,50,000, not ₹7,00,000. I used ₹1,00,000 so GTI is ₹7,00,000 and the later figures add up. Board calc top uses "₹7 lakh − ₹1 lakh" to fit the 18-character limit and keep the ₹ signs.

Checker: Line 4 / board 'Build GTI': 'Clubbing and set-off' leaves out brought-forward losses. Correct version: 'Club income, then set off current-year losses and set off brought-forward (carried-forward) losses. Adding up the result gives GTI.' On the board, write 'Clubbing, set-off and carry forward'.

Checker: Line 9–10: the ₹1,00,000 Chapter VI-A deduction only works under the old regime (opted out of s.115BAC). Under the default new regime, most Chapter VI-A deductions are not allowed; only a few remain, such as 80CCD(2) and 80JJAA. Add 'under the old regime' so the example isn't misleading.

Checker: Line 10: 'Tax rates apply on that figure' is loose. Total Income is first rounded off to the nearest ₹10 under s.288A. Income taxed at special rates, such as capital gains, is taxed at those rates and not at slab rates. Better: 'Tax is computed on this Total Income.'

Checker: Line 11–12: Agricultural income is exempt under s.10(1) and stays out of GTI and Total Income. For individuals and HUFs, though, it is added for rate purposes (partial integration) when the conditions are met. Add a short note so students don't assume it never affects tax.
Checker: Line 14: 'Gross is the garden, Total is the trimmed' doesn't read properly. Better: 'Gross is the full garden; Total is the trimmed garden.'
